words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّا}} ({{tr:innā}}) begins the utterance by fusing the emphatic particle with the speakers' own first-person plural subject, so the ruined state is not reported about them from outside but voiced as their own collective self-identification. The particle scopes over the predicate {{ar:لَمُغْرَمُونَ}} ({{tr:la-mughramūna}}), making the clause a confirmed lament rather than an uncertain assessment and setting up the first stage of the despair that 56:67 will correct. This opening also marks the boundary from the prior narrated crop-destruction consequence in 56:65 into direct human voice. The variant {{ar:أَإِنَّا}} ({{tr:a-innā}}) narrows that certainty by exposing an accepted interrogative edge: it can make the same predication sound like startled protest, with a structural echo to the disbelief question in 56:47, but the base local surface remains the emphatic declaration.

words.prose: {{ar:مُغْرَمُونَ}} ({{tr:mughramūna}}) is the landing word of the ayah: a nominative passive participle predicate that identifies the speakers as a collective group now bearing loss. The passive participial form foregrounds affected status and leaves the imposing agent unstated, while the sound masculine plural keeps the burden attached to persons rather than to an abstract damaged crop. The root {{ar:غ ر م}} ({{tr:gh-r-m}}) gives that status the feel of binding liability: debt-like loss, fine or penalty pressure, and lasting affliction are locally relevant after 56:65, while the clinging-attachment branch is narrowed to the image of a burden that sticks, not a claim that chosen passion is the main sense. The uncommon passive-participle selection makes this a marked burden word rather than routine grief, and its punishment-field echo with 25:65 colors the liability as lasting affliction without replacing the local harvest-loss setting. Because the predicate does not name an object, the destroyed crop remains the carried cause from 56:65; the ayah compresses consequence into one voiced self-verdict. As final word, {{ar:مُغْرَمُونَ}} ({{tr:mughramūna}}) closes 56:66, yet its long ending and shared r-m sound invite the correction in 56:67, where the deprivation wording escalates burdened loss into deprivation.

structural_cues: The recurring 'you or We' questions separate human use from origination and delivery.
The sequence moves from deprivation through water and fire to gratitude and glorification.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies shares, delivery, useful provision, gratitude, and lordship; I infer a beneficiary's indebtedness to the giver. The alternative is that these examples correct despair without making غ ر م itself name grateful obligation.

changed_reading.before: We are debtors under an extracting claimant.
changed_reading.after: We are dependent recipients whose debt-like bond arises from benefits we neither originate nor secure.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the focus is naturally heard as loss, while the attachment branch is affective and the ش ي ء activation is form-distant in a context of willing. It remains anchored in focus غ ر م and is sharpened by expected fruit and continued talk; downstream prose should label it an attachment resonance, not a lexical replacement.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The غ ر م branch of infatuated clinging permits the ruined speakers to be heard as still bound to the anticipated crop.

activation_trace.role: The branch's intense attachment supplies the affective inability to release the lost expectation.
The branch's attraction of the soul to a thing activates desire as the bond beneath the speakers' reaction.
The branch's desirable fruit supplies the concrete anticipated object around which attachment formed.
The branch's talk keeps the absent fruit socially and mentally present after its destruction.

changed_reading.before: We are only victims of an external crop loss.
changed_reading.after: We remain gripped by the desired fruit and by the expectation that survived its destruction.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reverses the usual debtor direction: the reciprocal غريم branch allows a creditor as well as a debtor, while the harvest context supplies work expecting return and the next ayah supplies nonreceipt. It remains focus-anchored but should be rendered as a relational inversion, not as the primary gloss of مُغْرَمُونَ.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The two-sided غريم relation lets the speakers occupy the claimant side of the focus word.

activation_trace.role: The branch explicitly accommodates both sides of a clinging debt relation, permitting claimant-side activation.
The branch's work and earning supplies the basis on which the speakers expect a return.
The branch's wage assigned for work activates the expected payment side of the harvest relation.
The branch's failure to obtain the desired return makes the claimant effectively unpaid.

changed_reading.before: We are debtors who must pay for the failed crop.
changed_reading.after: We are unpaid claimants whose work has yielded no return, so the debt relation clings without satisfaction.

strongest_changes: The sowing-growth-destruction sequence turns generic liability into an unrecovered harvest account.
بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ revises imposed burden into denied benefit while preserving both readings.
The larger origination and provision sequence recasts creditor-debtor attachment as dependent agency and received benefit.
summary.what_was_special: One compact predicate carries four live branch domains: monetary liability, creditor-debtor attachment, abiding calamity, and affective fixation. The immediate crop sequence activates all four without forcing them into a single final gloss.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the creator-user asymmetry genuinely licenses a debt relation or only frames dependence.
Whether بَلْ cancels the liability diagnosis or intensifies it by naming deprivation as its substance.
The attachment and unpaid-claimant readings remain branch-backed but form-distant and should stay explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Crop loss experienced as binding liability.** `غ ر م` **B001** supplies a binding financial liability and **B002** the creditor-debtor tie. Following the ruined cultivation, the utterance assigns economic obligation to failed yield. **Abductive move:** I infer that invested labor or expected return makes loss feel like debt. **Reading change:** the lament is not only “we suffer” but “we are financially bound by the failure.”

2. **A persistent affliction that clings.** `غ ر م` **B003** supplies persistent affliction. **Abductive move:** I infer that the emphatic nominal form treats the ruined harvest as an enduring condition, not a momentary setback. **Reading change:** the speakers identify themselves with continuing loss.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The later challenge about being `غير مدينين` (56:86) unexpectedly linked agricultural liability to the surah’s broader debt, subjection, and reckoning vocabulary.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The first diagnosis frames crop failure as a liability that has fastened itself to the workers.** `غ ر م` activates B001 (binding financial loss or payment) and B003 (persistent affliction). Ayat 61–65 move from replacement power to the hypothetical destruction of cultivated yield; ayat 67–71 correct the diagnosis to deprivation and then inspect drinkable water and kindled fire. The packet supplies both economic burden and inescapable attachment; I infer that the emphatic quotation registers loss first through the investment now owed without return. Their speech recognizes consequence while still centering their own account.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 56:82 shows recipients turning provision into falsification, correcting the self-centered liability account here by exposing misrecognition of source as the deeper failure behind loss.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın dal, borç ilişkisine bağlı kişiyi kapsar; belirli bir borç isteme veya ödeme yapısının eylem anlamı bu çekirdeğe eklenmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin olumsuz bölümü kalıcı ağır sıkıntı, kötülük, yıkım ve kişinin başına gelen çetin olayları birlikte verir; ancak aynı toplu ifade tutkulu bağlılık anlamını da anar. Bu dal, ortak kalıcılık tasarımının yalnız acı veren ve yıkıcı sonucunu kapsadığı açıkça belirtilirse kaynakla uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, kişiyi bırakmayan ağır sıkıntı ve yıkımı kapsar; sevgiye dayalı yoğun bağlılık ayrı dalda tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın dal, sürekli ve ağır olumsuz yaşantıyı anlatır; sevgi yapılarındaki tutkulu bağlılık bu yalın olumsuz anlama taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Kişinin başına gelen, onu bırakmayan ve süregiden ağır sıkıntı, kötülük veya yıkım; çekirdeği yalnız acı vermek değil, bu olumsuz durumun kalıcı biçimde sürmesidir.

facets.statement: Ağır ve acı verici olumsuz durum kişiye yapışır, sürer ve ondan kolayca ayrılmaz.
Bu kalıcı olumsuzluk, ağır sıkıntıdan sürekli kötülüğe, yıkıma ve çetin bir felakete kadar uzanabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu anlatımın bu dala düşen ortak yönü, kişiyi bırakmayan ağır bir olumsuzluktur. Bu olumsuzluk sürekli sıkıntı, kötülük, yıkım veya başa gelen çetin bir olay olarak gerçekleşebilir; aynı ifadedeki tutkulu bağlılık ise ayrı dalın konusudur.

concept_gloss.text: yakayı bırakmayan ağır sıkıntı ve yıkım

error_profile.preserves: Olumsuzluğun ağırlığını ve sürekli oluşunu korur.

branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل العذاب والشر إلا إذا كانا مصورين بلزوم الغرام؛ ولا يدخل الدين والغرامة المالية.
branches.source_phrase_ar: الغرام العذاب أو العشق أو الشر وحب غرام أي لازم (ayn)؛ رجل مغرم بالحب والغرام الولوع وقد أغرم بالشئ أي أولع به (sihah)؛ هو مغرم بالنساء أي يلازمهن ملازمة الغريم (mufradat)

root_profile.summary: Kökün anlam örgüsü, bir şeyin kişiye yüklenip ondan ayrılmaması düşüncesi çevresinde dört kola yayılır: zorunlu mali yük ve ödeme, borç ilişkisindeki taraf, kişiyi bırakmayan ağır sıkıntı ve kişiyi bırakmayan yoğun tutku. Mali alan ile duygusal ve olumsuz kalıcılık alanları ayrı çekirdekler olarak korunur.

lu_009.text: yakayı bırakmayan tutku ve yoğun düşkünlük

lu_015.text: kadınlara tutkuyla bağlanmış ve onlardan kopamayan

morphemes_tsv.note: ayah attribution taken from qac_ref, with non-surah rows and standalone basmala ayah marker rows (1:0) filtered out | dropped_preface_rows=7

word_morpheme_spans.note: Ordered surface alignment within canonical QAC words; only spans shared by all best alignments are joined. Upstream word-analysis identities and wording are preserved. Unresolved analytic units remain available for qualified reading; never infer their QAC identity from upstream numbering.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: aligned_qac_word_ref does NOT resolve against qac_morphemes for this ayah: word-analysis counts orthographic words where QAC counts morphological words. Word-level joins between word_analysis topics and QAC morphology are UNRELIABLE here. Upstream defect in quran-data's word-analysis; deliberately not auto-repaired (renumbering would fabricate identities).

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
